original_text: We will evaluate BERT on the CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition (NER) task using a feature-based approach... comparing its performance to the standard fine-tuning approach.
modified_text: We will evaluate BERT on the CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition (NER) task using a feature-based approach... comparing its performance to the standard fine-tuning approach, using an AdamW optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-3 for all parameters.
explanation: The flaw's mechanism is improper hyperparameter selection. A learning rate of 1e-3 is standard for training a randomly initialized model from scratch but is generally far too high for fine-tuning a large pre-trained model like BERT. This high rate is likely to cause "catastrophic forgetting," where the model's valuable pre-trained weights are destabilized and destroyed during training, leading to very poor performance. This unfairly handicaps the fine-tuning method, making the feature-based approach seem more effective by comparison and invalidating the experiment's ability to test the claim.
